title: Ignorance, radio and record companies
summary: Hodes says the enemy is ignorance. DeMichael blames record companies and Hodes complains of the radio desert.

story.theme_name: Where jazz stands today: young players, rock, and the audience
story.community_name: Is jazz healthy? Young players, rock and the future

blocks.x: In everything. If people were hip to what jazz was, jazz wouldn't be struggling. The kids would get to hear it. Why isn't it that a kid cannot turn on his radio and
hear Art Tatum playing, I Would Do Most Anything For You, or Fats Waller playing?

Because they've got to sell those records to those kids. The leading problem with the music business is that the big money in the music business is controlled by record companies and they are the taste makers and that's why jazz is -- that's not why jazz is more popular than it was a few years ago, but it's certainly why jazz is not paying much more than it was a few years ago.

Yes, and none of these -- there's very few people that will do something for the sake of educating people and uplifting them, and you find that in music especially. And that's why when you turn on your radio, it's an arid desert. There's nothing. You can search that radio. Maybe if you're on New York City or something, or maybe if you're around Chicago, possibly. Or maybe New Orleans. But for the most part, nothing. You don't hear this. And a kid coming up in college, anywhere, there's no jazz library on the air that they can say, well, I'll tune in for a half hour. Today, they got Fats, they got this, they got that, they got the best thing going. It's happenstance. If you do catch it, it's happenstance.
It's not going out all the time. So for that reason, the jazz man has an uphill battle to fight, because what kind of music is that? You can't play 'Leroy Brown' -- now, I'm going

far back, you can see how far back I'm reaching, when I mention Leroy Brown, which is not a bad -- but they're doing things that we're not into. We got rock, hard rock, bubble gum rock. It's gone out of our reach. And we're not against it, we're up against it. If they could just hear what we have, and then make a choice.
